chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from Ibn Sinān, from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who led a people in salat, then a nosebleed afflicted him after he had performed one rakʿah or two rakʿahs, so he put forward one who had prayed though one rakʿah or two rakʿahs had been missed by him. He said: he completes the salat with them, then he puts forward a man to give the salām for them, and he himself stands and completes the remainder of his salat.
The proper way regarding this report is that we carry it upon a kind of recommendation, even though indication by gesture is sufficient according to what was contained in the first report.

key_terms.أَمَّ: led the people as Imam in congregational salat
key_terms.رُعَافٌ: nosebleed that interrupts the Imam during salat
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: gives the salām concluding the salat

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if the Imam gets a nosebleed during congregational salat and appoints someone who missed rakʿahs to continue?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling for an Imam whose salat is interrupted by nosebleed after completing one or two rakʿahs. It states that a replacement may complete the congregational salat, while the original Imam later completes his own remaining salat; the compiler then notes that this should be understood as a recommended manner rather than an obligation.
